## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}

```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
data("penguins", package = "palmerpenguins")
summary(penguins)
nrow(penguins)
ncol(penguins)
```
` The penguins dataset describes the various characteristics (habitat and various physical characteristics) of three species of penguins Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo. Its key variables are: species, island, bill lengths and depth, body mass, flipper length, year and sex. The data includes 344 individuals and 8 distinct variables and the mean flipper length of the penguins is 200.9 mm.`

```{r}
penguin_scatterplot <- ggplot(data = penguins, 
       mapping = aes (x = bill_length_mm, flipper_length_mm, color = species)) + 
  geom_point()

penguin_scatterplot
```
```{r}
ggsave("flippervbill.png",
       plot = penguin_scatterplot,
       )
```
```{r}
set.seed(367) 
##This makes it so that the numbers are reproducible
```
```{r}
norm_sample <- rnorm(10)
##This generates a group with 10 samples form a standard Normal distribution
```

```{r}
Q2_df <- data.frame(
  norm_vec = norm_sample,
  log_vec = norm_sample > 0,
  char_vec = letters[1:10], #Generates "a" through "j"
  factor_vec = factor(c("low", "med", "high", "low", "med", "high", "low", "med", "high", "low"))
)
##This generates the data frame 
```
```{r}
mean(Q2_df$norm_vec)
mean(Q2_df$log_vec)
mean(Q2_df$char_vec)
mean(Q2_df$factor_vec)
```
